NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under City Council Meeting agendas at rhe.city and during regular
  business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's website and a
  recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP-TV Channel 35
  (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome in-person on any item during City Council consideration of the item. Public
  correspondence may also be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record. Members of the public may also comment online using
  eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos” page of the City’s website
  (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an “eComment” button next
  to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp page. After you
  register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen by the
  public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the record.

  An opportunity is also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 13, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:08 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN’s granddaughters.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and
  Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  Community Services Supervisory Pinuelas
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-M AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

M.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION TO AUTHORIZE THE CONTINUED USE OF

  ADOPTED RESOLUTION 2535 TO AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO
  CONTINUE TO IMPLEMENT AND UTILIZE TELECONFERENCE
  ACCESSIBILITY PROCEDURES TO CONDUCT PUBLIC MEETINGS
  PURSUANT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 361.

5.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PRESENTATION TO RETIRING COUNCIL MEMBER STEVEN ZUCKERMAN

MAYOR ZERUNYAN thanked and recognized COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN on his 25
years on the City Council, and briefly highlighted his many accomplishments.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN with gifts including a
commemorative hat, a City of Rolling Hills Estates street sign from City staff titled “Zuckerman
Way”, and a photo book encapsulating his 25 years on the City Council.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed his appreciation for the gifts, recognitions, staff,
and his City Council colleagues.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN introduced those present to make presentations to COUNCIL MEMBER
ZUCKERMAN:

  Representative Eric Ponce-Furlos thanked COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN on
  behalf of Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi for his 25 years of service.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 13, 2022
   MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented a scroll to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN on
  behalf of Los Angeles County Supervisor Janice Hahn.

  City of Lomita Mayor Barry Waite recognized COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN and
  presented him with a certificate of recognition.

  Rancho Palos Verdes Mayor Pro Tem John Cruikshank, as Chair of the South Bay Cities
  Council of Governments (SBCCOG) recognized COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

  Rosa Kwon Easton on behalf of the Palos Verdes Library District presented a certificate
  of recognition to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

  Matthew Brach on behalf of the Palos Verdes Unified School district recognized
  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

  Martin Gombert, on behalf of Palos Verdes Transit Authority presented COUNCIL
  MEMBER ZUCKERMAN with a commemorative bus award.

  Los Angeles County Fire Department Assistant Fire Chief Brian Bennett presented
  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN with a scroll.

  On behalf of the Clean Power Alliance, Ted Bardacke, recognized COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZUCKERMAN virtually.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN noted that certificates were also received by Congressman Ted
  Lieu, Senator Ben Allen, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Lomita Station,
  the City of Rolling Hills and the City of Palos Verdes Estates.

COUNCIL MEMBERS STEGURA, SCHMITZ, MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, City Manager
Grammar, City Attorney Davis and MAYOR ZERUNYAN each thanked COUNCIL MEMBER
ZUCKERMAN for the impact he’s had on each of them, and for his 25 years of service to the
City and Community.

6.  OATH OF OFFICE

The Oath of Office was performed by Assistant City Manager Davis for MAYOR PRO TEM
BRITT HUFF and COUNCIL MEMBER-ELECT PAM BROWN SCHACHTER.

7.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION & RECOGNITION OF OUTGOING MAYOR

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF thanked MAYOR ZERUNYAN for his service to the City of Rolling
Hills Estates and the greater community, and reviewed the many accomplishments achieved
during his term as Mayor during 2022.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN opened several gifts to thank him for his service and dedication, including
a commemorative Rolling Hills Estates pandemic mask, a framed photo of the Armenian
Genocide Dedication Ceremony, and an updated Mayoral Gavel Plaque listing his four terms
as Mayor.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF introduced those present to make presentations to MAYOR
ZERUNYAN:

  Representative Eric Ponce-Furlos thanked MAYOR ZERUNYAN for his year of service
  as Mayor.

  City of Lomita Mayor Barry Waite recognized MAYOR ZERUNYAN and presented him
  with a certificate of recognition.

  Rancho Palos Verdes Mayor Pro Tem John Cruikshank recognized MAYOR
  ZERUNYAN.

  Rosa Kwon Easton on behalf of the Palos Verdes Library District presented a certificate
  of recognition to MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 13, 2022
   Los Angeles County Fire Department Assistant Fire Chief Brian Bennett presented
  MAYOR ZERUNYAN with a scroll to recognize him.

  Matthew Brach on behalf of the Palos Verdes Unified School district recognized
  MAYOR ZERUNYAN.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF noted that certificates were also received by Senator Ben Allen,
Congressman Ted Lieu, Supervisor Janice Hahn, the City of Rolling Hills and the City of Palos
Verdes Estates.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN expressed his appreciation for the recognitions and for his fellow Council
Members and staff for their work and support throughout the year.

  MAYOR ZERUNYAN nominated MAYOR PRO TEM BRITT HUFF to serve as
  MAYOR.

The motion was approved by acclimation.

  MAYOR HUFF then nominated COUNCIL MEMBER VELVETH SCHMITZ to
  serve as MAYOR PRO TEM.

The motion was approved by acclimation.

MAYOR HUFF thanked the residents of Rolling Hills Estates for the privilege of serving on the
City Council and for being reelected, and thanked the City Council for supporting her as Mayor,
and for the years they have all worked together, especially getting through the pandemic.

  ***

At 8:13 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the meeting to a brief reception.

MAYOR HUFF called the meeting back to order at 8:38 p.m.

  ***

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Martin Gombert, Administrator for the Palos Verdes Transit Authority (PVTA), spoke regarding
the free New Year’s Eve bus services offered across the Peninsula.

9.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

10.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  EQUINE EMERGENCY SHELTERING AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council enter into the attached Agreement with the
  County of Los Angeles (Department of Animal Care and Control) for the provision of
  a physical facility to serve as an emergency public shelter at Ernie Howlett Park for
  large animals in the event of a major emergency or disaster.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN thanked staff for bringing forward this agreement, and noted
that Rolling Hills Estates has done agreements like this in the past.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA seconded COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’s sentiments,
and confirmed with the City Attorney that this contract does not replace one currently in
existence. She also confirmed with Management Analyst Slawson that the City’s Facility
Coordinator as defined in the contract would be Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith.
COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA also noted that during the last Park & Activities Commission

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 13, 2022
 meeting, Commissioner Persichina commented that Ernie Howlett Park was difficult to get
horses in and out of. Management Analyst Slawson explained that members of the Los
Angeles County Department of Animal Care & Control conducted two site visits to determine
ingress and egress of the park. The park and arenas are used daily for horses and horse shows
are held there, and with this information the Department of Animal Care & Control and
Superintendent Goldsmith felt comfortable with the facility being used for this purpose.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE AGREEMENT WITH THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  (DEPARTMENT OF ANIMAL CARE AND CONTROL) FOR THE PROVISION
  OF A PHYSICAL FACILITY TO SERVE AS AN EMERGENCY PUBLIC
  SHELTER AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK FOR LARGE ANIMALS IN THE EVENT
  OF A MAJOR EMERGENCY OR DISASTER.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 220504
  DETERMINATION THAT UNLISTED USE IS SIMILAR TO AND NOT MORE
  OBJECTIONABLE THAN USES ALREADY LISTED SECTION 17.04.030 OF THE
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  LOCATION: 712 DEEP VALLEY DRIVE

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive the staff memo, discuss the issues,
  and adopt Resolution No. 220478, determining that a tattoo and body piercing studio
  is similar to and not more objectionable than other services uses already listed in
  RHEMC Section 17.30.020, and determining that in accordance with the California
  Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code § 21000 et seq.: “CEQA”), the
  application is Categorically Exempt under Class 1, Section 15301 Existing Facilities.

Planning Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material). She noted the
following typographical error: the title of the Resolution should be “Resolution 2537, a
Resolution of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates…”

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS AMENDED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2537 AS AMENDED, DETERMINING THAT A
  TATTOO AND BODY PIERCING STUDIO IS SIMILAR TO AND NOT MORE
  OBJECTIONABLE THAN OTHER SERVICES USES ALREADY LISTED IN
  RHEMC SECTION 17.30.020, AND DETERMINING THAT IN ACCORDANCE
  WITH THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (PUBLIC
  RESOURCES CODE § 21000 ET SEQ.: “CEQA”), THE APPLICATION IS
  CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT UNDER CLASS 1, SECTION 15301 EXISTING
  FACILITIES.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Manager Grammer read Resolution No. 2537 by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 13, 2022
 C.  CALIFORNIA SPECIFIED GRANT FUNDS AUTHORIZING RESOLUTION FOR
  NATURE CENTER PROJECT APPLICATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2536 to approve all
  application documents for California Department of Parks and Recreation Office of
  Grants and Local Services Specified Grants Programs for the George F Canyon
  Nature Center project in the amount of $1.2 million and authorize staff to submit the
  application forms accordingly.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA thanked Senator Ben Allen for helping the City procure this
grant, along with all staff involved, Council Member Zerunyan and former Council Member
Zuckerman who assisted in the process.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2536 TO APPROVE ALL APPLICATION
  DOCUMENTS FOR CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF PARKS AND
  RECREATION OFFICE OF GRANTS AND LOCAL SERVICES SPECIFIED
  GRANTS PROGRAMS FOR THE GEORGE F CANYON NATURE CENTER
  PROJECT IN THE AMOUNT OF $1.2 MILLION AND AUTHORIZE STAFF TO
  SUBMIT THE APPLICATION FORMS ACCORDINGLY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Manager Grammer read Resolution No. 2536 by title.

D.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 220499
  DISCUSSION ITEM REGARDING THE AMENDMENT AND RESTATEMENT OF

  PERTAINING TO ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS
  LOCATION: CITYWIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file the informational item. Staff
  will return to City Council with an Urgency Ordinance for consideration at its meeting

Planning Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER BROWN SCHACHTER thanked Planning Manager Naughton for a clear
and thorough staff report.

Discussion ensued regarding overnight parking in relation to ADU’s and JADU’s.
